claims.text: Isolating Pt atoms within a less reactive Cu host weakens adsorption of reaction intermediates relative to aggregated Pt clusters.
Weaker intermediate adsorption on isolated Pt minimizes surface poisoning, including carbon deposition.
Isolated Pt in Cu enhances durability and selectivity relative to aggregated Pt clusters.
Low-loading Pt can be incorporated into supported Cu nanoparticles in a single-atom-alloy configuration.
Sufficiently high Cu-to-Pt dilution promotes individual dispersion of Pt atoms in the Cu matrix.
Changing synthesis conditions or metal ratios can instead produce small aggregated Pt clusters on Cu.
The Pt dispersion state produces a different electronic environment for isolated Pt than for clustered Pt.
Ligand and strain effects from the Cu matrix cause isolated Pt atoms to bind CO or hydrocarbon fragments less strongly than Pt clusters.
More optimal adsorption prevents excessive buildup of poisoning species and limits coking.
The proposed adsorption behavior limits particle sintering and thereby improves catalyst durability.
The single-atom-alloy catalyst will have lower activation barriers for key reaction steps than the clustered-Pt catalyst.
The single-atom-alloy catalyst will accumulate less carbonaceous material than the clustered-Pt catalyst.
The single-atom-alloy catalyst will degrade more slowly than the clustered-Pt catalyst.
The single-atom-alloy catalyst will maintain high selectivity toward desired products.
Aggregated Pt clusters bind intermediates more strongly and therefore deactivate more quickly through poisoning or sintering.
The hypothesis should apply when a less reactive host stably disperses noble-metal atoms and the reaction is sensitive to intermediate adsorption strength.
The hypothesis may fail if the host or reaction conditions alter atomic dispersion or if factors other than intermediate adsorption dominate the reaction mechanism.
The magnitude of durability and selectivity improvement depends on atomic dispersion, support effects, and reaction-specific factors.
